newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian soldiers to get air-conditioned tanks.
newsitem.headline: Australian soldiers to get air-conditioned tanks.

text.p: Soldiers defending Australia's tropical north are to have air conditioning fitted in their tanks to stop their ammunition exploding in the heat.
A report into the Australian army's performance in the Northern Territory found that the frontline city of Darwin had proved too hot for Leopard tank training exercises.
The National Audit Office report said temperatures inside the tank turrets could reach 63 Celsius (145 Fahrenheit), 30 percent above the recommended maximum.

"Without any cooling in the tanks, the high temperatures in northern Australia can cause inaccuracies in the gun sighting system and pose high risk to crew safety from heat-related injury," the report said.
It added: "The Army proposes to install a 'climate control system' for the Leopard tank to address these problems."
The army acknowledged in the report that high temperatures could cause equipment failure and "ammunition instability".
"This is because 105mm tank ammunition is proofed at 56 degrees Celsius," it said.
The Leopard tank was designed and manufactured in Germany for use in European conditions and in armoured warfare against the Warsaw Pact threat of the Cold War years.

The tank regiment was only recently relocated to Darwin as part of an army push to increase its presence in the country's remote north. The report said one tank squadron had already returned to the cooler climes of southern Australia because of the heat problems.
The air conditioning should be installed by the middle of next year.
